newsitem.title: INDIA: Canada hopes telecoms will boost trade with India.
newsitem.headline: Canada hopes telecoms will boost trade with India.

text.p: Canada hopes to boost trade with India through high-technology exports, particularly telecommunication equipment, following a telephone service contract won by Bell Canada, Canadian officials said Friday.
"We see telecom equipment as an area of huge potential," Canadian High Commissioner Stanley Gooch said.
Canada is the ninth-largest foreign investor in India.
Bell Canada and India's Tata group have jointly won a licence to provide telephone services in southern Andhra Pradesh state.
Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said Indian Communications Minister Beni Prasad Varma had assured him of India's decision to pass a law to empower a telecommunications regulator.
"The minister indicated that there would be legislation dealing with a regulatory authority," Axworthy said.

The Tata-Bell consortium had joined other license winners in opposing what they termed as high charges for private companies to connect to the network of the state-run Department of Telecommunications, India's telephone monopoly.

India opened up telephone services to private firms under an economic reform programme launched in 1991. Gooch said he expected Canada to export environmental technology and aircraft as well as newsprint, wood pulp and fertilisers.
Canada expect India to export more computer software to add to traditional exports of textiles, jewelry and pharmaceuticals, Gooch said.
Bilateral trade totalled C$1.0 billion ($750 million) in 1995, Gooch said, adding that India had a surplus of C$100 million ($75 million).
Canada will open diplomatic offices in the Indian cities of Calcutta and Chandigarh, Canadian officials said. Canada already has a trade office in Madras, in addition to its embassy in New Delhi.
